newsitem.title: USA: Ohio wheat rated 46 percent good to excellent.
newsitem.headline: Ohio wheat rated 46 percent good to excellent.

text.p: Ohio's winter wheat crop was rated 46 percent good to excellent in the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its first weekly report of the year.
Wheat was rated four percent very poor, 13 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 35 percent good and 11 percent excellent. That was below national averages of 70 percent good to excellent, USDA reported.
"Farmers began fieldwork in earnest during the last half of the week as 3.4 days were rated suitable for fieldwork," the report said.
Farmers applied fertilizer but very little planting was completed. Less than one percent of the corn crop was planted as of Sunday, compared with nil for the five-year average.
Topsoil was rated nil very short, one percent short, 65 percent adeqaute and 34 percent surplus.
Pasture was rated two percent very poor, seven percent poor, 42 percent fair, 41 percent good and eight percent excellent.
